title: How Many Cells Equal the Largest Number of the Range?

concept.title: A node stores the maximum of its block and how many times it occurs; merging adds the counts when the maxima are equal
body: A row of numbers changes one cell at a time, and a question asks: **how many cells in the range `x..y` hold the largest value of that range?** For `3 7 7 2 7` the largest value of the whole row is 7 and it occurs 3 times; in the cells 1 to 4 it occurs 2 times. Looking up the maximum first and counting afterwards needs two passes over the range.

Store in every node the pair `(maximum, count)`: the largest value in the block and the number of cells that have it. A leaf is `(value, 1)`. To **merge** two nodes `(m1, c1)` and `(m2, c2)`: if `m1 > m2` the result is `(m1, c1)`; if `m2 > m1` it is `(m2, c2)`; if they are **equal** the result is `(m1, c1 + c2)`. The neutral node is `(-infinity, 0)`. The merge is associative, so the usual tree works.

body.code:
def merge(p, q):
    if p[0] > q[0]: return p
    if q[0] > p[0]: return q
    return (p[0], p[1] + q[1])            # equal maxima: the counts add up

NEUTRAL = (-INF, 0)
# a change sets the leaf (y, 1) and recomputes the parents; a question merges the blocks of the range

body: The same shape of node answers "the minimum and how many times", "the greatest value and the sum of its positions", and many other combined questions in one pass. Each operation costs O(log n).

statement: A row of `n` numbers is given. Process `q` operations: type 1 `x y` sets the number at the position `x` to `y`; type 2 `x y` asks how many numbers among the positions `x` to `y` are equal to the largest number among those positions. Print the answers to the questions on one line, in order.
inputFormat: The first line has `n` and `q`: the number of cells and the number of operations.
The second line has `n` numbers: the cells.

Each of the next `q` lines has three numbers `t`, `x` and `y`. If `t = 1`, set the cell number `x` to the value `y`. If `t = 2`, print how many cells from `x` to `y` are equal to the largest value in that range.
outputFormat: Print one number for every operation of type 2, separated by spaces.
constraints: Cells are numbered from 1; for a question 1 <= x <= y <= n.

examples.note: The maximum 7 occurs three times in the whole row and twice in the cells 1..4: 3 2.

hints: When two maxima are equal, add the counts.

explanation: Each node stores the maximum of its block and how many cells have it; merging keeps the larger maximum or adds the counts when the maxima are equal, and a question merges the nodes covering the range.
solution.complexity: Time O((n + q) log n), space O(n).
